macroCpi.title: NISR Macro Inflation & Rural-Urban Divergence
macroCpi.divergenceExplanation: Smallholder rural consumers face a 49.5-point higher price index than urban Kigali (273.2 vs 223.7). Thin secondary market liquidity, inter-district freight costs, and post-harvest depletion push rural staple food prices up disproportionately, underscoring the necessity of spatial arbitrage and local storage.

national.intro: District market-price signals for each crop, with the source, date and evidence behind every signal. Districts without approved data show as unavailable rather than being guessed.

national.tableCaption: Districts and their current market signal
national.ruleTitle: How the market signal is calculated
national.ruleText: The average price of the last 3 observed months is compared with the 3 observed months before. A rise of 10% or more is moderate; a rise of 20% or more is high. Any other change is low. The rule looks at the last 9 calendar months. A district needs at least 6 observed months in that window, and its latest price must be no more than 4 months old. Older data never produces a signal.

agronomic.title: NISR SAS Production & Input Adoption Audit
agronomic.leakageAdvice: Yield underperformed climate & input expectations (z < -1.75). When certified seed prices spike, substitution with uninspected farm-saved seed increases pathogen risks (bacterial wilt, degeneration). Verify RAB certification tags and avoid unsealed agro-dealer packets.
agronomic.climateAdvice: Yield constrained by rainfall deficit. Prioritize coordinated furrow irrigation in marshland networks, apply organic mulch to limit soil evaporation, and stagger planting cycles.
agronomic.intensificationAdvice: Strong synergy between certified seeds, balanced fertilizer, and hillside erosion control. Maintain post-harvest drying standards to prevent aflatoxin contamination.
agronomic.nominalAdvice: Yield and input utilization align with historical structural baselines. Continue standard agronomic practices and cooperative market aggregation.

arbitrage.title: Diesel-Adjusted Spatial Arbitrage Solver
arbitrage.intro: Evaluates origin-to-destination trade spreads between farm-gate prices (P_O) and terminal markets (P_D), subtracting distance-dependent diesel freight impedance and perishability spoilage.
arbitrage.sliderHelp: Simulate corridor profitability across fuel price policy scenarios:

howToRead.title: How Spatial Arbitrage is Computed
howToRead.body: For each corridor, round-trip freight is modeled as (2 * distance * 0.32 L/km * Diesel Price) / 5,000 kg + handling. Net margins subtract freight and commodity-specific transit spoilage (e.g. 8% per 100km for perishable tomatoes, 1.5% for potatoes, 0.5% for grains). Corridors earning over 40 Rwf/kg warrant dispatching surplus; those below 10 Rwf/kg should be held for local sale.

mathSection.title: Mathematical Formulations & Causal Foundations
mathSection.subtitle: Auditable, structural formulations implemented across AgrIntel's analytical engines without black-box heuristics (Charter Section 4):

forecast.title: Price outlook

auditMethod.title: MINAGRI Input Subsidy Leakage & Econometric Frontier (Section 4.2)
auditMethod.formula: Ŷ = Ȳ_base · Φ_climate(R_d,s, T_d,s, DrySpell) · Ψ_inputs(Seed_rate, Fert_rate)
auditMethod.residual: e_d,c,s = Y_obs - Ŷ, with standardized z-score z = e / σ_d,c
auditMethod.leakage: Leakage / Quality Risk: z < -1.75 AND Fertilizer adoption > 50% AND Climate Factor ≥ 0.85
auditMethod.climate: Agro-Climatic Stress: z < -1.75 AND Climate Factor < 0.85 (rainfall deficit / drought)
auditMethod.sampling: Calibrated with NISR Seasonal Agricultural Survey (SAS) Multiple Frame Sampling (MFS) weights.

arbitrageMethod.title: Diesel-Adjusted Spatial Arbitrage Optimization Solver (Section 4.3)
arbitrageMethod.formula: Π(O, D, c) = P_D · (1 - δ_c) - P_O - [d_O,D · β_fuel · P_diesel / Q_load + τ_mkt + κ_handling]
arbitrageMethod.burnRate: Medium goods truck fuel consumption: β_fuel = 0.32 L/km (5,000 kg payload capacity)
arbitrageMethod.shrinkage: Transit perishability shrinkage (δ_c): Tomato 8.0%, Irish Potato 1.5%, Maize & Grains 0.5%
arbitrageMethod.fuelPolicy: Regulated pump price: Rwf 2,927 / L vs Unsubsidized counterfactual: Rwf 3,600 / L (Rwf 673/L subsidy shield)
arbitrageMethod.breakeven: Fuel Breakeven Price: P*_diesel = [(P_D · (1 - δ_c) - P_O - τ - κ) · Q_load] / (d_O,D · β_fuel)

methodology.accuracyNote: Errors come from re-running the method on past months, using only data available at each point. Lower is better. No accuracy figure is shown unless a backtest produced it.
methodology.noEvaluations: No backtest results are recorded yet. Run the forecast pipeline to produce them.
limits: Empirical datasets are loaded from official NISR Seasonal Agricultural Surveys (SAS 2024A–2026B), WFP HDX retail market observations, Tangabid farmgate records, and CHIRPS / Meteo Rwanda subnational stations.
The outlook is a national average across monitored markets. It does not describe any single district.
Econometric residual models and spatial arbitrage corridors represent statistical optimization frontiers and should be paired with field extension verification.
Forecast ranges are based on historical volatility and holdout backtests. They are not absolute guarantees.
Advisory guidance is general information. Fertilizer doses and veterinary treatment are out of scope and need expert review.
Kinyarwanda translations are maintained with 100% key parity across all analytical modules.

dataLifecycle.title: 3-Tier Data Velocity Lifecycle & Production Automation
dataLifecycle.subtitle: How AgrIntel ingests live subnational data across differing velocity cadences without manual code intervention or app redeployment.
dataLifecycle.juryQuestionText: NISR releases CPI every month, WFP updates rainfall every 10 days, and SAS comes out every season. What happens when new data drops?

columns.automation: How New Data Is Handled Automatically

tiers.name: Tier 1: High-Frequency
tiers.datasets: WFP & TangaBid market prices (P_O, P_D), CHIRPS subnational rainfall anomalies (rfq), and RURA regulated diesel pump prices.
tiers.automation: A lightweight scheduled GitHub Action (.github/workflows/data-sync.yml) triggers every Monday at 05:00 UTC. It pulls updated feeds, recalculates Net Spatial Arbitrage Margins across 1,570 corridors and subnational Climate Stress Factors, and executes idempotent upserts into Neon PostgreSQL without model retraining.

tiers.name: Tier 2: Medium-Frequency
tiers.datasets: NISR Consumer Price Index (CPI) and Producer Price Index (PPI) series with Urban vs Rural food inflation decomposition.
tiers.automation: Ingested on the 10th of each month upon official NISR publication, updating the macro food inflation deflator (17.2% YoY) and recalibrating the rural-urban cost-of-living spread (Rural 273.2 vs Urban 223.7).

tiers.name: Tier 3: Structural Baseline
tiers.datasets: NISR Seasonal Agricultural Survey (SAS Seasons A, B, C) district production, harvested areas, and input adoption rates (certified seed, fertilizer, irrigation, anti-erosion).
tiers.automation: When NISR publishes seasonal surveys (Season A in April/May, Season B in October), the pipeline appends new district observations, re-estimates the econometric production frontier coefficients (Φ_climate, Ψ_inputs), and recalculates standardized residuals (z) to flag subsidy leakage risks below z = -1.75.

dataLifecycle.liveDemoNote: The 'Simulate Data Update' server action in the Alerts module demonstrates this live execution: inserting a price/climate revision into Neon, validating checksums, refreshing risk previews, and generating bilingual draft alerts.
